name: South Dakota WIOA Title I Youth Program
org: South Dakota Department of Labor and Regulation
what_you_do: Eligible teens meet a state staff member, take an assessment and make an employment plan. The state then gives youth job services. The program page does not list the services.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 24 and allowed to work in the US. Live in South Dakota or a nearby county. In-school youth ages 14 to 21 must be low-income and have a barrier such as basic skills deficient, English learner, homeless, in foster care, pregnant or parenting, or have a disability. Out-of-school youth must be 16 to 24.
pay_detail: Not stated on the program pages. The manual says the program is not an entitlement and depends on funding.
duration: Not stated on the program page.
deadline_text: No deadline posted on the program pages.
how_to_apply: Call 605-773-3101 (TTY 711) to ask where to start. Under 18, a parent or guardian must sign the application forms.
notes: Narrow: not every teen qualifies. The state may limit how many in-school youth it enrolls because at least 75 percent of funds go to out-of-school youth. Rules are from the state WIOA manual, section 4.1, revised October 2026. The state says all Title I youth also sign up for Wagner-Peyser job services. The manual also lists Selective Service registration rules (policy 4.6) that this card does not cover.
